Future Continuous Tense and Future Perfect Tense

You use the Future Continuous tense to talk about an unfinished action or event that will be in progress at a time later than now.
You use the Future Perfect tense to refer to a completed action in the future.
The Future Continuous tense is made up of two parts:
the simple future of the verb "to be" + the present participle (base + ing)
The Future Continuous tense can also be used to project ourselves into the future.
The Future Perfect tense is also made up of two parts:
the simple future of the verb "to have" (will have) + the past participle of the main verb
When you use this tense you are projecting yourself forward into the future and looking back at an action that will be completed some time later than now.
You often use the Future Perfect tense with a time expression.
Some people in engineering will be moved to construction and they will be considering redundancies too.
I'll be sitting in meetings all afternoon. I'll have a look tonight.
You will have left the office by the time it finishes but I'll have a look tonight.
Tag Questions
A tag question is a statement that is followed by a mini-question. You use a tag question to ask for confirmation.
Tag questions are used to mean “Do you agree?” or “Is that right?”
The basic structure is:

images.text:
Allen: Hi Joseph. Your lunch looks delicious. Leftovers?
Joseph: My wife outdid herself. Last night's seafood lasagna was spectacular.
Allen: Did you hear about the latest deadline? I'm really concerned that we'll not be able to finish the project in time.
Joseph: Yes, I was in this morning's boardroom meeting. It sounds like the accounting department is concerned about excessive spending, doesn't it? They seemed pretty agitated when we were discussing the need for new equipment.

Allen: Absolutely! They always have their eye on the bottom line. The CFO also mentioned that we will need to make some changes within the company. Some people in engineering will be moved to construction and they will be considering redundancies too. I think the company is struggling financially.
Joseph: Finding a permanent, stable job in this industry is a challenge, isn't it? The housing market is so unstable.
Allen: I agree. I'm on a one-year contract. Maybe I should start looking for other employment.
Joseph: It might not be a bad idea. If you like, I'll forward you an e-mail I received from a colleague who works for Constructionzone when I finish lunch. They are looking for someone.

Allen: Another contract? I'd be hesitant to simply change for change's sake.
Joseph: I believe that it is a permanent job. They are desperate to fill the position.
Allen: Sounds interesting. I'll be sitting in on meetings all afternoon. You will have left the office by the time it finishes, but I'll have a look tonight. You have my new e-mail address, don't you?
Joseph: AllenShaw@Webuild.net, right?
Allen: Correct. I'll be looking forward to reading the position description. It sounds like a great opportunity. Thanks!
